The World of Darkness is our world, but worse — gothic-punk, oppressive, where shadows are deeper and corruption runs through every institution. Vampires (called Kindred) have walked alongside humanity for millennia, hidden behind a code of secrecy called the Masquerade. The current era is the modern nights — the late 2020s, the Information Age made hostile to monsters who require darkness.

The First Tradition: Reveal not your true nature to those not of the Blood; doing so renders you forfeit to the wrath of your elders. The Masquerade is not just a law — it is the load-bearing beam of Kindred existence. Every vampire, regardless of sect, understands that exposure means a global pogrom they cannot survive.

The Beast is the predator within — not a metaphor but a literal supernatural entity riding inside every Kindred. It hungers, it rages, it remembers no laws but the chase. The Hunger is the Beast's primary expression: a constant gnawing pressure for mortal blood that rises with each scene, each act of exertion, each moment of Discipline use.

Kindred physiology: dead but animate, sustained by Vitae (vampire blood). The body does not age, does not breathe (unless willed), has no heartbeat (unless willed), runs cold to the touch. With recent feeding, Kindred can pass for living — flushed cheeks, warm skin, even sexual function. Without feeding, they appear corpse-like. Vulnerabilities are absolute.

The Embrace is the act of creating a new vampire: the sire drains the mortal nearly to death, then forces the mortal to drink the sire's Vitae. The mortal dies and rises within nights as Kindred. The Embrace is governed by the Second Tradition (Domain) and the Sixth (Destruction) — most sects regulate it strictly, requiring permission from the local Prince/Baron.

The Camarilla — the Ivory Tower — is the largest Kindred sect, founded in the 15th century to enforce the Masquerade and protect Kindred from mortal hunters. Its membership is conservative, hierarchical, and elder-dominated.

The Anarch Movement is the Camarilla's primary opposition — a loose coalition of younger Kindred, defectors, and clans who rejected elder rule. Born from medieval revolts and reignited in the 1944 Second Anarch Movement (Los Angeles), the modern Anarchs have been transformed by V5's clan defections: Brujah and Gangrel left the Camarilla en masse, joining the longtime Anarch core.

The Sabbat — Sword of Caine — is the third major sect, though largely absent from V5's main play. Where the Camarilla treats vampirism as a curse to be hidden, the Sabbat embraces it as divine: they are Caine's chosen, monsters by sacred design, opposed to the Antediluvians (whom they believe will return to consume their descendants in Gehenna).

The Second Inquisition is the most consequential mortal threat to Kindred in centuries — a coordinated alliance of intelligence agencies (FBI Special Affairs Division, MI5, Mossad, others), Vatican operatives, and inheritor remnants of older hunter organizations who pooled their data after early-21st-century leaks revealed Kindred existence to mortal agencies.

Clan Brujah — the Learned Clan, the Rabble, the Rebels. Once philosopher-kings of ancient Carthage, the Brujah were broken when their dream-city fell to Rome (with Ventrue help, a grudge they have not forgotten in two thousand years). Modern Brujah are passion incarnate: revolutionaries, activists, brawlers, intellectuals who lead with their fists.

Clan Gangrel — the Outlanders, the Beasts. The most feral of the great clans, Gangrel have always been closer to the Beast than other Kindred — closer to the wilds, closer to the animal. They wandered with Roma, with First Nations, with frontier outcasts, claiming no city-domain when they could claim the road.

Clan Malkavian — the Lunatics, the Madmen, the Oracles. The Malkavians are the most cursed of the great clans: their Antediluvian Malkav broke their Embrace itself, leaving every Malkavian afflicted with some form of derangement, divine madness, prophetic compulsion, or fractured perception.

Clan Nosferatu — the Hidden, the Sewer Rats, the Secret-Keepers. Their curse is absolute: every Nosferatu Embrace transforms the body into something monstrous — twisted, lumpen, fanged, often boil-covered or tumor-marked, always unmistakably inhuman. The Nosferatu Bane prevents them from passing for human in any context, which means they cannot move freely in society.

Clan Toreador — the Artistes, the Divas, the Roses. The Toreador are vampires in love with beauty, obsessed with art, sensation, beauty in all its forms. They are seducers, patrons, performers, critics, museum directors, fashion designers, opera singers, social butterflies, salonnières.

Clan Tremere — the Warlocks, the Pyramid, the Usurpers. The Tremere are the youngest of the great clans, formed in the 11th century when a cabal of mortal mages successfully transmuted themselves into vampires through an ill-understood ritual that involved the diablerie of the Salubri Antediluvian.

Clan Ventrue — the Blue Bloods, the Kings, the Patricians. The Ventrue have ruled Kindred society longer than any other clan; they founded the Camarilla, they typically hold the Princedom in any Camarilla domain, they manage the long centuries of mortal banking, real estate, politics, finance. They are the establishment. They are old money — older than the money itself.

Clan Banu Haqim — formerly the Assamites, the Children of Haqim, the Judges. An ancient clan from the Levant, the Banu Haqim were originally vampire-killers and judges: Kindred who killed other Kindred who broke ancient laws, enforcing balance through diablerie and execution. For centuries they were Independent, then Sabbat-aligned briefly, then Independent again.

The Hecata are the unified clan of the dead — formed when the Giovanni, Cappadocians, Lamia, Samedi, and other death-touched bloodlines merged in the 21st century to survive. They specialize in necromancy (the Discipline of OBLIVION in V5, shared with Lasombra), wraith-binding, soul-trafficking, and the long art of holding territory without sect protection.

Clan Lasombra — the Magisters, the Shadow-Bound, the Keepers. A clan of patrician shadows, ruthless schemers, and Mediterranean nobility, the Lasombra spent five centuries as the political backbone of the Sabbat — and then, in the 21st century, executed one of the most consequential clan defections in modern Kindred history: they crossed to the Camarilla, abandoning the Sword of Caine for the Ivor...

The Ministry — formerly the Followers of Set, the Setites, the Tempters. Once a clan worshipping Set, the Egyptian god of darkness, the Ministry has rebranded itself in the modern nights into a more flexible religious-political organization that recruits across all faiths and traditions, united by the conviction that liberation comes through the breaking of false constraints — every law, every fai...

Clan Tzimisce — the Dragons, the Old Country, the Fiends. A clan of monstrous Eastern European nobility, descended from boyars and warlords of the Carpathian Basin, the Tzimisce are flesh-shapers, soil-bound, and territorial to a degree no other clan matches.

Clan Ravnos — the Charlatans, the Wanderers, the Curse-Bearers. Once a clan of South Asian and Roma origin, masters of illusion and itinerant trade, the Ravnos suffered a near-extinction event in 1999 known as the WEEK OF NIGHTMARES: their Antediluvian Zapathasura awakened, the clan was driven to internecine slaughter in a global suicide-frenzy, and the surviving population was reduced to a tiny s...

CAITIFF: the clanless. Embraced by Kindred whose own clan-blood was too thin or whose Embrace failed to imprint clan-curses, Caitiff have no Bane, no clan-disciplines (they can learn any common Discipline, with effort), and no clan-status. They are universally scorned by clan-bound Kindred who consider them bastards or accidents. The Anarchs accept them more readily than the Camarilla.

Disciplines are the supernatural powers granted by Kindred Vitae. Each clan has three (sometimes four) signature Disciplines they learn naturally; Kindred can learn other Disciplines by drinking the blood of one who possesses them, but the cost in Vitae and time is significant. MAJOR DISCIPLINES:

BLOOD BOND (Vinculum): a Kindred or mortal who drinks from the same Kindred source three nights becomes mystically devoted to that source — they will defend their regnant, obey them, love them in a way that overrides reason. The bond runs from drinker to source. ONE DRINK: the drinker thinks fondly of the source. TWO DRINKS: the drinker is genuinely emotionally attached.

Kindred must feed on mortal blood to survive. Standard feeding: Kindred bites a mortal, drinks (typically in small amounts to avoid kill or detection), uses fangs to seal the wound. The mortal feels euphoria during the bite (most clans), often forgetting the experience or remembering it as a vivid dream.

HUMANITY (V5) is a measure of how human the Kindred remains — how connected to the moral framework of mortal life. Humanity ranges 0-10 (most starting characters at 7). Higher Humanity = more empathy, fewer frenzies, more ability to pass for living (eat food at low levels, sleep at human hours, even sexual function with feeding).
A Camarilla domain (or Anarch city, with structural variations) is governed by:

The JYHAD is the eternal war of the elders — a centuries-spanning game of chess in which Antediluvians, Methuselahs, and ancient elders manipulate younger Kindred as pieces. Most political conflicts in Kindred society are downstream of someone's Jyhad ploy.
